commands.notes: Output: one OfficeConversionReport per input file, written as each file finishes (parallel work runs on background tasks and reports through the pipeline thread with Write-Progress); -Plan returns one OfficeConversionPlan; -SaveJob returns the job FileInfo; -AsString returns string. Errors per file are non-terminating with the input as target object and FullyQualifiedErrorId {DiagnosticCode},Convert-OfficeDocument; -FailOnLoss turns loss into a per-file error. -To values (OfficeFormat, also accepts an extension such as .odt or docx): Pdf, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Markdown, Html, Rtf, Text, Csv, OpenDocument (odt/ods/odp chosen from the source family) and the explicit Odt, Ods, Odp, Epub, AsciiDoc, Latex, Confluence (ADF), OneNote, Visio (.vsdx from .vsd). Legacy upgrades use the same targets: .doc -To Word, .xls -To Excel, .vsd -To Visio. Image targets (PNG, JPEG, SVG of pages, slides, sheets or diagrams, including the pdf-png and visio-svg routes) go through Export-OfficeDocumentImage. Google Docs/Sheets/Slides uploads need an authenticated session and are not file outputs; they stay with their format areas. Routing: source format from -From or content detection plus extension; target from -To or the -OutputPath extension; route from -Route or the catalog. Options objects are routed by type, so one call can carry New-OfficeWordPdfOptions and New-OfficeExcelPdfOptions for a mixed folder; hashtables follow one rule: a hashtable whose keys are all source format names (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Pdf, Markdown, Html, Rtf, Text, Visio, OpenDocument ...) and whose values are hashtables or options objects is format-keyed, so @{ Word = @{ PageSize = 'A4' }; Excel = @{ UseWorksheetPrintAreas = $true } } configures each source family of a multi-route run; any other hashtable is flat and its keys set the matching properties on every selected route's options; a key that no selected route can use is an invalid argument; route-specific .NET option types without a factory (OdgToPdfOptions, VisioToPdfOptions, XpsToPdfOptions, ChmConversionOptions, DjVuToPdfOptions, PublisherReadOptions, IWork/OneNote/AsciiDoc/LaTeX options) are passed the same way. Batch: -Path accepts files, wildcards and folders; -LiteralPath binds Get-ChildItem output. -Resume and the saved-job set share one checkpoint format; -SaveJob writes the same OfficeBatchOptions JSON that Studio and the CLI open, so saved jobs remain portable. Absorbs from this area: ConvertTo-OfficeDocument, Export-OfficeDocumentPdf, Export-OfficeConversionJob (-SaveJob), Invoke-OfficeConversionJob (-JobPath), New-OfficeConversionOptions (-Options plus the common parameters), ConvertFrom-OfficeImage (-Document with an OCR review, or -Path with -Ocr). Absorbs from other areas (mapped by their agents): Word ConvertFrom-OfficeWordHtml, ConvertFrom-OfficeWordMarkdown, ConvertTo-OfficeWordDocument, ConvertTo-OfficeWordHtml, ConvertTo-OfficeWordMarkdown; Excel ConvertTo-OfficeExcelHtml, ConvertTo-OfficeExcelWorkbook; PowerPoint ConvertTo-OfficePowerPointHtml; PDF ConvertFrom-OfficePdfHtml, ConvertTo-OfficePdfExcel, ConvertTo-OfficePdfHtml, ConvertTo-OfficePdfMarkdown, ConvertTo-OfficePdfPowerPoint, ConvertTo-OfficePdfWord; markup ConvertFrom-OfficeAsciiDocMarkdown, ConvertTo-OfficeAsciiDocMarkdown, ConvertFrom-OfficeLatexMarkdown, ConvertTo-OfficeLatexMarkdown, ConvertFrom-OfficeMarkdownHtml, ConvertTo-OfficeMarkdownHtml, ConvertFrom-OfficeIWork, ConvertFrom-OfficeOneNote, ConvertFrom-OfficeOpenDocument, ConvertTo-OfficeOpenDocument, ConvertFrom-OfficeRtf, ConvertTo-OfficeRtf. Options factories routed through -Options (owned by their areas): New-OfficeWordPdfOptions, New-OfficeExcelPdfOptions, New-OfficePowerPointPdfOptions, New-OfficeMarkdownPdfOptions, New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions, New-OfficeMarkdownPowerPointOptions, New-OfficeRtfPdfOptions, New-OfficeHtmlPdfOptions, New-OfficeTextPdfOptions, New-OfficeWordOpenDocumentOptions, New-OfficeExcelOpenDocumentOptions, New-OfficePowerPointOpenDocumentOptions, New-OfficePdfWordOptions, New-OfficePdfPowerPointOptions, New-OfficePdfExcelOptions, New-OfficeHtmlConversionOptions. Views: Document = OfficeDocumentReadResult; Text = plain text per document (new projection over blocks; replaces Get-OfficeImageText and the PDF text readers); Markdown = page-aware Markdown per document, or OfficeDocumentPageMarkdown per page with -ByPage (was Get-OfficeDocumentPageMarkdown); Json = the reader's versioned JSON (was -AsJson); Chunks (Get-OfficeDocumentChunk); Hierarchy (Get-OfficeDocumentHierarchy); Structure (Get-OfficeDocumentStructured); Tables (Get-OfficeDocumentTable); Visuals (Get-OfficeDocumentVisual); Assets (Get-OfficeDocumentAsset); Ingest = one ReaderIngestResult for the whole selection (Get-OfficeDocumentIngest); Ocr = recognition review with per-page words, confidence and reconstructed layout, which Convert-OfficeDocument -Document turns into Word, Excel, HTML or CSV (was Get-OfficeImageDocument). Writing tables, visuals or assets to disk is Export-OfficeDocumentAsset, so Read- has no file-system effect. Asset filters (Kind, MediaType, Extension) moved to Export-OfficeDocumentAsset; for listing use Where-Object. Multiple files, wildcards and folders read in parallel with -ThrottleLimit, results stream as each finishes, failures are non-terminating ReadError records (replaces Get-OfficeDocumentBatch, its -ContinueOnError and -BatchOptions). Candidate absorptions from other areas (decided by their agents): Read-OfficePdf and Get-OfficePdfText (design consolidation table), Get-OfficeWordText for plain extraction. Folder and wildcard selection stops at 500 files by default; -MaximumFiles raises the cap (0 = no limit), the same parameter Convert-OfficeDocument and Search-OfficeDocument use. -Password opens encrypted sources; per-format load options in -Options can still carry their own passwords.

map.reason: A recognized image is one more conversion source: the OCR review from Read-OfficeDocument -As Ocr converts through the same command, routes and reports as every other file, or -Path scan.png -Ocr does both steps.
ConvertTo- is reserved for object-to-text conversions; file-to-file conversion is Convert-OfficeDocument with the fixed parameter vocabulary, per-file reports and -ThrottleLimit/-Resume.

A saved job is a serialized Convert-OfficeDocument batch, so -SaveJob on the same command keeps one parameter vocabulary for running and saving; the job file format shared with Studio and the CLI is unchanged.
PDF is one target of Convert-OfficeDocument; the design replaces Export-OfficeDocumentPdf there, and the seven per-format options parameters become one type-routed -Options.
Reading a saved data file into objects uses the Import- verb; the report belongs to Convert-OfficeDocument runs as well as saved jobs.
Route fidelity and limits stay available as the Conversion set of the single capability command, next to read and protection capabilities.
Get-Office{Format} names now open documents for editing; reading content for search and AI ingestion is Read-OfficeDocument, which was already this command's alias.
Assets are one view of Read-OfficeDocument; writing them to disk is Export-OfficeDocumentAsset so the read command has no file-system effect.
Read-OfficeDocument accepts many paths, wildcards and folders and reads them in parallel, so a separate batch command is a duplicate.
Chunks are a view of the same read; the Folder set is covered by -Path accepting folders.
Format detection is part of a document's info; one command answers what a file is and what it contains.
Hierarchical chunks are a view of Read-OfficeDocument.
Folder ingestion is the Ingest view over a folder selection.
Page Markdown is the Markdown view; an existing read result is re-projected through the InputObject set.
Structured extraction is a view of Read-OfficeDocument.
Tables from any format are a view of Read-OfficeDocument; writing CSV/Markdown/JSON files is Export-OfficeDocumentAsset -Type Table. Rows of an .xlsx table are read with Import-OfficeExcel -Table.
Visuals are a view of Read-OfficeDocument; writing them is Export-OfficeDocumentAsset -Type Visual.
Recognizing an image's layout is the Ocr view of Read-OfficeDocument, with OCR settings in one New-OfficeOcrOptions object.
Text from an image is the Text view of Read-OfficeDocument with OCR; the same call reads text from every other format.
Package security inspection is a validation check that never changes the file, so it belongs to Test-OfficeDocument -Check Security.
Protection support per format is one more capability catalog; one command lists read, conversion and protection capabilities.
Commands that work on any format use the Verb-OfficeDocument{Noun} pattern.
Running a saved job is Convert-OfficeDocument -JobPath, so saved and ad-hoc batches share reports, -Plan, -RetryFailed and checkpoint reuse.

The bundle only grouped per-format options with a few general settings. Convert-OfficeDocument takes the per-format options objects directly through -Options and the general settings as parameters, and -SaveJob serializes them into the same job file.
Cross-format options factories are named New-OfficeDocument{Purpose}Options, matching the Read-OfficeDocument -HierarchyOptions parameter.
DSL aliases exist only for commands used inside a content block and need a format prefix; ConvertTo-OfficeVisual prepares an object outside a block, so it keeps only its command name.
The alias name becomes the command itself; Get-OfficeDocument is retired.
